# Instructor guide · Topic 13: Trees

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Read and describe trees (root, parent, child, leaf, depth, height, subtree), traverse them four ways, and write recursive tree functions with confidence.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **Tree vocabulary:** A tree is a hierarchy: one root, and every other node has exactly one parent.
- **Trees in Python:** A tree node is a tiny class with a value and two child pointers.
- **Depth-first traversals:** Preorder, inorder and postorder all go deep first.
- **Breadth-first: level order:** A queue visits the tree level by level.
- **Thinking recursively about trees:** Almost every tree problem has the same shape: handle None, ask both subtrees for their answer, combine with the current node.
- **Bottom-up tricks: height, diameter, balance:** Some answers need information from both subtrees at once.

## Duration and prerequisites

- Lessons: about **58 minutes** of guided material (6 lessons)
- Practice: 23 coding problems and 31 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 10 (Recursion & Backtracking), Topic 8 (Queue & Deque)

## Live coding demonstrations

- Nodes and the helper (lesson “Trees in Python”)
- The template (lesson “Thinking recursively about trees”)
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Balanced Tree: height at every node → one bottom-up pass** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: Tree anatomy: click any node · Tree traversals

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- Leaf?
- Depth vs height?
- Edges in a tree of n nodes?
- Preorder / inorder / postorder?
- Level order uses…
- Tree recursion template?
- Diameter trick?

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Preorder Traversal (`t-preorder`)
- Inorder Traversal (`t-inorder`)
- Postorder Traversal (`t-postorder`)

Code tracing on the board: Preorder (`t-p1`), Inorder (`t-p2`), Postorder (`t-p3`), Level order (`t-p4`)

Find-the-bug warm-ups: Crash at the bottom (`t-d1`), Counting nodes, minus some (`t-d2`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- Level Order Traversal (`t-level-order`)
- Diameter of a Binary Tree (`t-diameter`)

## Homework

- Balanced Binary Tree (`t-balanced`)
- Right Side View (`t-right-view`)
- Maximum Path Sum (`t-max-path`)
- Finish the topic's Review quiz in the browser and clear the revision queue.

## Solutions and grading

- Reference solutions: `solutions/13_trees/` (also behind “Show solution” in the browser).
- Students check their own work with `python dsa.py test <id>`; collect `pytest tests/test_my_solutions.py -k trees` output as evidence.
- Grade with the coding rubric in [README.md](README.md#grading-rubrics).
